# Glossary

These words are used in one sense throughout the series. If a chapter needs a second sense, it says so.

| Term | Meaning in this book |
|---|---|
| Risk $R(f)$ | Expected loss of a predictor under the data law. Not the training loss. |
| Empirical risk | Average loss on a named sample. Say which sample. |
| Estimator | The procedure, including preprocessing and selection. |
| Estimate | The number that procedure returned on one sample. |
| Bayes predictor | A minimizer of the risk over a rich class, for a named loss. |
| Approximation error | The gap from the Bayes predictor to the best function in a restricted family. |
| Estimation error | The gap from that best function to the one you fit. |
| Baseline | A simpler procedure on the same split and metric. A constant predictor counts. |
| Split unit | The entity a random split must not tear apart: row, patient, document, or time. |
| Leakage | Use of information the decision-time system will not have, including test labels and future events. |
| Validation | Data used to choose knobs. Not a license to also be the published test. |
| Test | A measurement of a procedure that was already frozen. |
| Proper score | A score minimized in expectation by stating the true probability. Log loss and Brier score are examples. Accuracy is not. |
| Calibration | Among cases given predicted probability $p$, about a fraction $p$ are positive. |
| Inductive bias | What an architecture or penalty makes easy, stated as a restriction. |
| Known case | An input with an answer you can compute without the experiment. The harness must pass it. |
| Shift | A named change in a law: of $X$, of $Y$ given $X$, or of the mixture of slices. |
| Threat model | Who may change an input, under which budget, with what knowledge. |
| Safety case | Hazards, controls, evidence, assumptions, and a withdrawal condition. |
| Reproduction | The same claim and protocol, within a predeclared tolerance. |
| Upstream | A book you read under its own license. Not a chapter of this book. |
